record.original_question: Which mathematically consistent fractional-calculus models should be used to formulate quantum mechanics with nonlocality in space and quantum field theory with nonlocality in space-time by passing from lattices with long-range interactions to their continuum limits?

evidence.quote: Quantum mechanics with nonlocality in space and quantum field theory with non-locality in space-time by using models of lattices with long-range interactions and its continuum limits [145, 146, 147, 148, 149, 150, 151, 152, 153, 154] are important future direction of applications of FC to quantum physics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a lattice model in d-dimensional space (or space-time) whose degrees of freedom interact through long-range couplings of power-law type, i.e., interaction strengths between sites n and m decaying as |n−m|^{-(d+α)} for some parameter α > 0. By taking an appropriate continuum limit of such lattice systems (with lattice spacing tending to zero), one is led to continuum field equations that involve fractional (nonlocal) differential operators, such as the Riesz fractional Laplacian (−Δ)^{α/2} or fractional time derivatives.

Problem: Identify a mathematically consistent fractional-calculus framework — specifying (a) which classes of fractional derivatives and integrals (e.g. Riesz, Caputo, Marchaud, Grünwald–Letnikov, or generalized fractional operators on appropriate function spaces), (b) which functional-analytic setting (domains, boundary/decay conditions, distributional or Sobolev-type spaces), and (c) which quantization scheme — that:

1. Formulates a quantum mechanics with spatial nonlocality, obtained rigorously as the continuum limit of lattice Hamiltonians with power-law long-range interactions, in a way that preserves self-adjointness of the Hamiltonian, unitarity of time evolution, and the correct local limit as α → 2.

2. Extends to a quantum field theory with nonlocality in space-time, obtained as the continuum limit of lattice field theories with long-range interactions in both spatial and temporal directions, satisfying basic consistency requirements (e.g. well-defined propagators, causality or its suitable nonlocal replacement, locality recovery in a prescribed limit, and renormalizability or finiteness properties).

Determine such fractional-calculus models and rigorously justify the lattice-to-continuum limit linking them to long-range interacting lattice systems.
artifact.category_tag: Fractional calculus and nonlocal quantum field theory
artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as a future research direction rather than a precise conjecture. While various fractional Schrödinger equations (Laskin) and nonlocal field theories with fractional Laplacians have been proposed and studied, no single universally accepted, mathematically rigorous fractional-calculus framework derived from continuum limits of long-range lattice systems for both nonlocal quantum mechanics and nonlocal QFT has been established. The problem is therefore best classified as open.

status_evidence.title: Fractional quantum mechanics and Lévy path integrals (Laskin)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces fractional Schrödinger equation via Riesz fractional Laplacian, a partial model for spatial nonlocality.
status_evidence.claim: Fractional QM exists for the spatial case, but a unified rigorous framework matching lattice continuum limits and extending to QFT is not established.

status_evidence.title: Tarasov, Fractional dynamics of systems with long-range interactions
status_evidence.snippet: Derives continuum fractional equations as limits of lattice models with long-range interactions; discusses open extensions to quantum and field-theoretic settings.
status_evidence.claim: The continuum-limit program is developed classically and proposed as a direction for quantum and QFT extensions, indicating the question remains open.
